refutes.statement: The local improvement lemma LIL of k4/c4min_reduce.md §5.3 (#51) without the core's private-goods rule: every configuration without a valid owner has an M1, M4 or M5 move raising (r', -t, Lam)

notes: x = agent 0 (goods 1, 2, 3 private: the only broken core condition), tau1 = agent 1, tau2 = agent 2; all three are big-top (10 > 5 + 4) and share their top 0. At key (0 frozen on agent 0) the configuration Q1 = {4,5}, Q2 = {7,8}, pool {1,2,3,6} has t = 1, is pool-optimal, has no valid owner, and no M1/M2/M4/M5 move (#51's k4/red_lil.py) and no pool/cycle(any pairs, keep)/two-agent/downgrade move (#53's k4/gap_model.py) raises (r', -t, Lam). The global maxima of (r', -t, Lam) are (2, 0, 18) at the keys of agents 1 and 2, both completable. So the statement 'every maximum is completable' survives here; only the local lemma fails. Re-derived with three implementations (k4/suite/model.py for the static facts).
